title: Annotatio III §.X (4): Faith of the first centuries — if they taught Transsubstantiation, Jews and Gentiles would have hissed at once
pass_a_gloss: (4.) Both to the Faith, and to the praxis built upon it, of the first Christians through many centuries: For if the earliest Christians had professed Transsubstantiation, none of them then being ignorant of the true sense of Christ’s words This is my body, this is my blood, how could it ever have been that the rumor of the dogma would not most swiftly, without any delay, have passed from these otherwise fervent defenders of their Religion’s Mysteries to the Jews and Gentiles among whom they lived — about to meet not only their serious contradictions but every kind of hissing?
pass_b_english: (4) Faith and praxis of the first centuries: if the earliest Christians had professed Transsubstantiation, none then mistook ‘This is my body / blood.’
That dogma’s rumor would have flown at once to neighboring Jews and Gentiles and met not only contradiction but every hiss — from such fervent mystery-defenders it could not have stayed quiet.
source_text: (4.) Tàm Fidei, quam huic superstructæ praxi, primorum, per multa secula Christianorum: Quodsi enim primævi Christiani Transsubstantiationem professi fuissent, nemine eorum tùm temporis, veri sensus Christi verborum: Hoc est corpus meum, hic est sanguis meus, ignaro existente, quî fieri unquam potuisset, quò minùs ab his, præfervidis alioquin Mysteriarum Religionis suæ propugnatoribus, fama dogmatis, ad eos, quos inter vivebant, Judæos pariter atque Ethnicos, quam velocissimè transiisset citra omnem moram, non contradictiones horum ferias duntaxat, sed & exsibilationes quascunque expertura?
